questions.question: Seven friends P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are watching a cricket match sitting in a stadium. P is sitting at one extreme end, T is sitting second to the right of P and to the immediate left of U. V is sitting between Q and U. Q is sitting to the immediate left of S. Who is sitting at the extreme right end?
questions.solution:
1) As P is sitting at the extreme end and T is sitting second to the right of P, P must be at the left end of the row.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30e782965d8077162e1c2b9ca705155ef633cc6b771411f8b714d4ab3c464b4f.png] 

2) T is sitting immediate left of U.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb31248ef51a6c62bbc028ec411c3f291fc550ff95d0ec482268c0df43fd06f7.png] 

3) V is sitting between Q and U.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6aa52d90d8cbc9f2074334150b4cbec4022786e80f4711848cd0979fd9e89a44.png] 

4) Q is sitting to the immediate left of S.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1cc9da9f673143eb129cea5c9e11cce3805a610c1856e89c197147ee4c77f43.png] 

5) R is sitting at the remaining position that is exactly between P and T.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b9c92ff62b9ba899af9869dbcd8b9c5d363df2f5da244b6a95feb33230633d9.png] 

Hence S is sitting at the extreme right end.

questions.question:
The statements given below are followed by two conclusions labelled I and II. Assuming that the information in the statement is true, even if it appears to be at variance with generally established facts, decide which conclusion(s) logically and definitely follow(s) from the information given in the statements.

Statements:

All guns are flowers.

All swords are flowers.

Conclusion I: Some swords are guns.

Conclusion II: No sword is a gun.

options.text: Either conclusion I or conclusion II follows.

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/063ff23dfee066f18533d256d8a58ade2af2a814384168c7ea1104be75225063.png] 

**Conclusion:**

I. Some swords are guns → False (It is possible but not definite)

II. No sword is a gun → False (It is possible but not definite)

Both conclusions form a complementary pair.

Hence, either conclusion I or conclusion II follows.

questions.question: In a certain code, NOON is written as 5665. How will SOLOS be written in that code?

Logic for word NOON,

N → 14; 1 + 4 = 5; So N is coded as 5

O → 15; 1 + 5 = 6; So O is coded as 6

NOON → 5665

Similarly,

S → 19; 1 + 9 = 10; So S is coded as 10

O → 15; 1 + 5 = 6; So O is coded as 6

L → 12; 1 + 2 = 3; So L is coded as 3

Thus SOLOS is coded as 1063610.

questions.question:
If ‘A’ is replaced by ‘+’, ‘B’ is replaced by ‘-’, ‘C’ is replaced by ‘÷’ and ‘D’ is replaced by ‘×’, find the value of the following expression.

17A19B2D24C8
questions.solution:
Using BODMOS

 
 

 
 
Letter

 
 
 
A

 
 
 
B

 
 
 
C

 
 
 
D

 
 
 

 
 
Meaning

After decoding the equation is

17 + 19 - 2 × 24 ÷ 8

= 17 + 19 - 2 × (24 ÷ 8)

= 17 + 19 - (2 × 3)

= 17 + 19 - 6

= 36 - 6

= 30

Hence, 30 is correct answer

questions.question:
Select the option that will correctly replace the question mark (?) in the series.

1, 2, 11, 36, ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

Difference between consecutive numbers is square of odd numbers.

2 -1 = 1 = 1²

11 - 2 = 9 = 3²

36 - 11 = 25 = 5²

So, difference between 36 and next term is square of 7 i.e. 49

36 + 49 = 85

Hence, next term in the series is 85.
